result.summary: The street environment provides basic pedestrian infrastructure with continuous sidewalks and signalized traffic control at the intersection. However, the lack of marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb extensions creates a higher-risk environment for those crossing the street.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: The signalized intersection at Ontario St lacks painted crosswalks, reducing driver awareness of pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left curbsides near the intersection

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the sidewalk path, narrowing the effective walking width.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks at all legs of the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by preventing parking too close to the intersection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a wide, unobstructed concrete sidewalk directly adjacent to a two-lane roadway. While the walkway is continuous and in fair condition, there is a lack of physical buffering from traffic and the building frontage is largely opaque due to security shutters.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane with no physical separation like trees, planters, or parked cars.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line separating the sidewalk from the asphalt roadway.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The use of security shutters and solid walls at the ground level reduces natural surveillance and creates a less inviting pedestrian environment.
hazards.location_in_image: Ground floor of the brick building.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Installing street trees or large planters would provide a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, improving both safety and comfort.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions or Parklets
interventions.description: Adding curb extensions or repurposing space for parklets could narrow the perceived roadway and provide more space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Improved Street Lighting
interventions.description: Enhancing lighting levels, particularly at the pedestrian scale, would improve visibility and perceived safety near the blank building frontage.

result.summary: This residential street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, though they are occasionally obstructed by utility poles. The environment lacks marked crossings and traffic calming, while parked cars create potential sightline issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible for a long stretch of the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both curbs block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the walking path, narrowing the effective width.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks to provide safe and visible crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility around parked cars.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential area.

result.summary: The image depicts a two-way urban street with residential row houses and a prominent vacant lot. While a sidewalk and on-street parking are present, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian crossing infrastructure in the immediate mid-block area.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parallel parked vehicles along the curb can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of oncoming motorists.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The large vacant lot creates a gap in the active streetscape, reducing natural surveillance and potentially making pedestrians feel less secure.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, the vacant lot area

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the nearby intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Streetscape Activation
interventions.description: Encourage infill development or temporary community use of the vacant lot to improve natural surveillance and street vitality.
